question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 140 km/h and 80 km/h. The length of one train is 340 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 11 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains in opposite directions = 140 + 80 = 220 km/h.

Convert speed to m/s: 220 × (5/18) = 1100/18 m/s.

Total distance covered = Speed × Time = (1100/18) × 11 = 12100/18 ≈ 672.22 m.

Length of the second train = Total distance − Length of first train = 672.22 − 340 = 332.22 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 332.22 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 140 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 80 km/h

Length of first train (L₁) = 340 m

Time taken to cross each other (T) = 11 seconds
